content.title: About
content.content: Veggie burger is a plant‑based patty made from a blend of vegetables, legumes and whole grains, shaped into a burger and served on a soft bun. It offers a tasty alternative to traditional meat burgers, suitable for vegetarians and anyone looking to reduce meat consumption.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The patty provides over 30% of its calories from plant protein, mainly pea and soy isolates.
Common ingredients include carrot, beetroot and spinach, giving the burger a vibrant color and extra vitamins.
Oats or quinoa are often added to improve texture and moisture retention.
A gluten‑free version is possible by using a gluten‑free bun and grain‑free binders.
Many recipes are fortified with B‑vitamins and iron to match the nutritional profile of meat.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Pea and soy protein support muscle growth and repair, providing a complete amino acid profile.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with beef, the burger contains mostly poly‑ and monounsaturated fats that are heart‑friendly.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole grains add dietary fiber, aiding digestion and promoting satiety.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The burger supplies vitamin A, vitamin C, iron and potassium, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Environmental benefits
items.content: Plant‑based burgers require less water and land than beef, resulting in a lower carbon footprint.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Soy protein is a common allergen; individuals with soy sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: To enhance flavor, the burger may contain added salt; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Gluten (if regular bun is used)
items.content: A standard wheat bun introduces gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Processed ingredients
items.content: Some versions include preservatives and flavor enhancers; choose minimally processed options when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the veggie burger on a warmed bun with lettuce, tomato, onion, mustard or ketchup. For extra crunch, grill or pan‑sear the patty before assembling.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the fresh burger refrigerated at 0–4 °C for up to 3 days. Frozen versions store for up to 3 months; thaw in the refrigerator before cooking.
